en: Preface to the *Nyāyapraveśa-śāstra* (The Treatise on Entering Right Reasoning):

The fundamental cause of all phenomena is called "right reasoning" (*nyāya*). That which penetrates the fundamental cause of all phenomena is called "right knowledge" (*samyagjñāna*). Reasoning is manifested through knowledge; the thesis (*pakṣa*) relies upon the illumination of reasoning.
Knowledge serves as the means of entry, while right reasoning is the object of entry. When a Bodhisattva realizes true direct perception (*pratyakṣa*), [they enter therein].

Through inference (*anumāna*), there exist true means of establishment (*sādhana*) and true means of refutation (*dūṣaṇa*). By means of wisdom one illuminates the principles, and thereby awakens oneself and others;
hence it is called "The Entrance into Correct Principles through Logic" (*Hetuvidyā-praveśa*). For example, by establishing *tathatā*, one enters the correct principle of *tathatā*;

by establishing *vijñaptimātra*, one enters the correct principle of *vijñaptimātra*; and by establishing impermanence, one enters the correct principle of impermanence. If one is not a person who has realized the truth, then...
Once the mouth is opened, thirty-three [objections] follow in succession. How difficult it is to establish a formal syllogism (*pramāṇa*)!

It is like the principle that when ritual, music, military expeditions, and punishments issue from the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords fold their hands and await his commands, and thus the world is well-governed.

But when these matters issue from the feudal lords and great officers, the four barbarian tribes invade one another, and the people have no place to set their hands or feet. Therefore, upon reading this treatise...
It is like a commoner perusing the genealogies of emperors; though he may know the order of the ancestral lineages, he cannot claim descent from the divine progenitors.
Or it is like one who knows every article of the Three Thousand Penal Codes, yet, not being a judicial official, seeks to impose punishment upon the guilty—who would submit to such a verdict?
Therefore, what the student most urgently requires is the task of realizing the Truth; the task lies in realization.
Truly so! Inscribed by the True Dharma Layman Feng Mengzhen of Xiushui.
